dedupe_keys.name: electrical grids and load shedding modeling commons netlogo model of grid frequency after a generator failure

description: A NetLogo model of how an interruption event changes the frequency of an electrical grid and how it recovers, published on Modeling Commons. Contents: houses (demand) and one generator (supply) linked radially, with Hz and frown agents as visual aids; sliders set the number of houses and the power available; the stages of generation, failure, recovery and stabilisation can be run together or one at a time and are plotted. It is framed on the three US interconnections and the 60 Hz requirement, citing an EIA note. Producer: Jane Antonas. Coverage: an abstract single-generator grid. Format and access: NetLogo 6.3.0 file (Electrical_Grids_and_Load_Shedding.nlogo, uploaded 4 December 2023) that runs in the browser or in NetLogo. Licence: not stated on the pages read. Caveats: one generator, random blackout assignment and no location-based load shedding; the author lists extensions such as multiple generators and renewables. Simulation uses: teaching frequency response to supply-demand imbalance and load shedding. Related records: none identified.
